sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 26.0% a year from $4,319 million in FY2016 to $34,639 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F231].
The path was a step change rather than a smooth climb: revenue rose 68.3% in FY2021 and 43.6% in FY2022, then fell 3.9% in FY2023 before recovering 13.7% and 34.3% [D258][D314][D370][D426][D483].
The FY2022 jump included the Xilinx acquisition, which added Embedded revenue of $4.6 billion against $246 million in FY2021 [S110][S109][P41].
The FY2023 decline came from a 25% fall in Client revenue on weak PC demand and inventory correction, partly offset by Embedded [P35].
FY2025 growth was driven by Data Center and Client and Gaming, with Data Center revenue up 32% to $16.6 billion [P15].
Data Center is now the largest segment at 48.0% of revenue and contributed 15.7pp of the 34.3% FY2025 growth [D692][D694][D483].
That growth came from strong demand for EPYC processors and Instinct GPU accelerators [P13].
Client and Gaming added 19.0pp in FY2025, with Client revenue up 51% on a 31% rise in processor unit shipments and a 15% rise in average selling price [D701][P10].
Operating income grew 94.4% against revenue growth of 34.3%, an incremental operating margin of 20.3% [D484][D483][D511].
Diluted EPS rose 165.0% against net income growth of 164.2%, as the diluted share count was flat at -0.1% [D487][D485][D506].
Operating margin of 10.7% in FY2025 sits above the 7.2% window median but far below the 22.2% FY2021 high [F60][D795][D794].
Gross margin reached a window high of 49.5%, up 0.2pp, with cost of revenue adding only 0.2pp to operating margin [F40][D498][D513].
Gross margin gains were limited by roughly $440 million of net inventory and related charges tied to the MI308 export control [P14].
SG&A took 1.2pp off operating margin as it grew 48.9% against revenue growth of 34.3% [D515][D503][D483].
Net margin of 12.5% exceeded operating margin of 10.7%, helped by $577 million of other income from unrealized investment gains and a $103 million tax benefit [F80][F60][P5][P4].
Operating cash flow of $7,709 million was 1.78x net income, and free cash flow of $6,735 million was 1.55x, against a window median of 1.17x [F110][F70][D470][F130][D471][D810].
Free cash flow margin of 19.4% in FY2025 sits just below the FY2021 window high of 19.6% [D467][D803].
Operating cash flow was reduced by a $2.2 billion inventory build to support the Data Center ramp [P3].
Capex of $974 million was 2.8% of revenue and 1.87x D&A, the highest ratio in the window [F120][D466][D472].
Net cash reached $6,456 million, or 18.6% of revenue, the 100th percentile against six semis peers whose median is -13.9% [D476][D477][D826][D827].
Total debt rose 138% to $4,096 million after the March 2025 issuance of $1.5 billion of notes [D475][D508][P6].
Buybacks of $1,316 million were 19.5% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 0.1% [X150][D479][D506].
Return on average equity of 7.2% ranks at the 17th percentile against a peer median of 26.7% [D482][D830][D831].
Operating margin of 10.7% is at the 17th percentile against a semis peer median of 31.0%, despite revenue growth of 34.3% [F60][D818][D819][D483].
Total debt rose 138% in FY2025 to $4,096 million, though net cash still rose to $6,456 million [D475][D508][D476].
Days inventory outstanding climbed to 165 days from 160, extending a rise from 106 days in FY2022 [D481][D424][D312].
The effective tax rate moved -21.3pp to -2.5% on an $853 million release of uncertain tax positions, a one-period item [D469][D412][P4].
If operating margin holds above the 7.2% window median, the FY2025 recovery is durable; a slip back toward the 1.8% FY2023 level would reverse it [D795][F58].
Watch days inventory outstanding against the 165-day FY2025 level; a further rise would signal demand lagging the Data Center build [D481].
Watch net cash against the $6,456 million FY2025 level, given the 138% debt increase, in the FY2026 10-K [D476][D508].
